# THE DEUTERONOMY WALK — the fifth book in order from 1:1 (the owner: "start with deuteronomy", 2026-09-15, after NUMBERS CLOSED)

The owner's words (2026-09-15): "lets plan for deut next. where do we start" (the plan given: commit, the rereads, the measurement, the reading of
chapters 1-3, the compile; the readback's design his decision), "commit push" (29d477a), "I don't need to compact. read what you need to get ready",
"start with deuteronomy". This file is the walk's map: one section per sitting, the coverage computed at each close, the owed items named where
they are found. The rulings that govern it are the Numbers walk's (World/step9/NUMBERS_WALK.md; the memory numbers-in-order-ruling.md): READ THEN
COMPILE PER PORTION, never read ahead; CHAPTER NUMBERS, never portion names; the parashah grain; the spine Onkelos whole + the Sifrei on
Deuteronomy where it has a piska BY POSITION (logic/CORE_SHELF.md's spine default of 2026-08-27).

THE WALK'S FORM (the derivation era's, THE_STEPS Steps 2-5): each portion is one READING SITTING — the measurement passes first (the shelf by
position, both files' row counts, every row's first citation, the four-form scan for rows outside the span, the parser on every verse, the frames
and the register, the prior reads, the drafts' spans, the store's token counts and glosses), then the ink as asserts run all at once, then the rows
(Onkelos per verse; the Sifrei per row in both files, the middah named), then ONE ledger written by one script with coverage computed, the
display layer's override rows patched from the ink's own literals, the manifests with every check cut from the store's bytes, the seat script,
the rituals in sequence, the fold predicted and matched, the stamp row, the records — then a COMPILE SITTING (the design in this file before code;
probes to fail; the docket; the runner; the tape; every gate with the register gate --strict; the sweep). THE READBACK (THE_LOOP.md's STEP 6) is
designed at this book on the owner's word — Deuteronomy is the tape read back, the speech retelling what the tape holds.

THE SHELF ON DEUTERONOMY, MEASURED (sitting 1): the Sifrei on Deuteronomy's export holds 357 piskaot and 2,357 rows in BOTH files, and NO

⚠ THE LESSONS OF 1b: (i) a fast checker over the runner's ink and census asserts (parts exec'd without the callee imports) saves the four-minute
import cycle per typo — build it before the first run; (ii) generate the CASES literals from the cells' own asks by script, then freeze them (a
mistyped expected string grades nothing); (iii) the daemon gate reads LITERAL submits only — unroll the scene's loop; (iv) the engine writes a
daemon's effects AFTER it returns: a one-block open-and-close is the daemon's own write, stamped as the engine would; (v) sum the daemon's watches
for the writes count — the design's prose miscounted; (vi) the counter's first long walk moves every checkpoint that reads the timers' list order or
their pending state (CP6, CT2, CT4, CT6, CX6) — read pending timers in due order, and grep the checkpoints for `pend` before predicting; (vii) a
parser mark is not a word: strip the marks before any word match (the slot stamp); (viii) the register gate's CHAPTER class covers a run citation
whose chapter holds a closed entry — predict the gate's class from its code, not from the reading's sense; (ix) two period timers of one effect on
one day break a join keyed on the day alone — key on the value; (x) the scratch forms compute ROOT by git rev-parse, and the INK namespace must
carry _ROOT; (xi) a probe's expected verse form must be a tape position (the Zered's closer 21:10-13, not 21:12); (xii) compare fires by day number,
not by an era's date — the tape's early fires predate the exodus.

## THE FOUR-RUN RULE (owner-ruled 2026-09-16 at 3b's close — "Yes write it")

THE FOUR-RUN RULE (owner-ruled 2026-09-16, "Yes write it"): a sitting is FOUR RUNS, a clean compaction point after each — (1) the rereads, the measurements, the design in the map; (2) the docket (the scan, the verdicts in parts, the writer); (3) the types, the runner, the stitch, the tape to 10/10; (4) the gates chain, the records, the forms — each near 150-200k tokens, never one run of 600k; a reading sitting split the same way (the measurements and the ink; the rows and the ledger; the seat, the chain and the fold; the records). Inside a run: the docket's rows read at a short cut; a prior sitting's form derived by sed and read only where it differs, never whole; the state doc's checkpoint at each run's end names the next run's first step. [AMENDED 2026-09-17: "the docket's rows read at a short cut" STRUCK on the owner's word — THE WHOLE-ROW RULE, the map's tail.] The next sitting (chapter 6's reading, or the schema sitting) opens by naming its four runs; sitting 3b (one run, ~600k) is the case that ruled it.

## THE WHOLE-ROW RULE (owner-ruled 2026-09-17: "OK, never ever cut corners with the Talmud go back and fix the ones where the shortcut was taken and write it in the rules forever") — written between 4b's RUN 2 and RUN 3

THE WHOLE-ROW RULE (owner-ruled 2026-09-17: "never ever cut corners with the Talmud"): EVERY ROW OF THE SHELF — Talmud, Mishnah, Tosefta, the spine's books (the Sifrei and its kin), Onkelos — IS READ WHOLE BEFORE ITS VERDICT IS TYPED. No character cap on a row, ever; no verdict from a row's opening; a range read is every row of the range whole. The four-run rule's "short cut" clause (2026-09-16) is STRUCK: a docket takes as many runs as its whole reading needs (the run count yields, the clean point after each run stands); a prior sitting's SCRIPT is still derived by sed and read where it differs — that economy is on our own text, never on the shelf's. THE CUTS TAKEN ARE REREAD WHOLE AND CORRECTED: a corrected verdict on an uncommitted docket by an overlay in its part (the cut's verdict kept beside it as the record); a correction to a committed ledger or docket by an APPENDED section (append-only); a cell typed from a cut row retyped from the whole one. THE MEASURE THAT RULED IT: the first forty rows of chapter 6's docket reread whole against their 170-character verdicts — two verdicts wrong, one row carrying another row's content, nine notes short of the row's point.

WHERE THE CUT WAS TAKEN (measured on the record before the fix): (1) SITTING 4b — chapter 6's docket, all 747 rows printed at 170 characters (708 rows longer than the cut; the dump 407,226 characters); (2) SITTING 4 — the Sifrei's 67 spine rows printed with the English capped at 1,500 characters and the Hebrew's opening 150 (seven rows past the cap: 31:1, 31:4, 31:6, 32:7, 32:18, 36:1, 36:2; the ledger COMMITTED at a7955cc); (3) SITTING 3b — the docket's part C (rows 140-209) printed at 650 characters on the record (fifteen rows longer), the other parts' print not on record (82 of 275 rows longer than 650; the docket COMMITTED at 7c8554e); (4) SITTINGS 2b AND 1b — the instrument existed with N a parameter and the print not on record (2b: 114 of 327 rows longer than 650; 1b's dump in the scratchpad); the link rows of 1b-3b "read whole" by their parts' own headers. Before the four-run rule (2026-09-16) — the Numbers walk's dockets — every row was read whole from the dump by the parts' own headers.

THE FIX (in this order; each chunk's corrections on disk before the next is read): (a) chapter 6's docket reread whole in chunks of forty rows on ch6_docket_rows.py with N = 100000; each part carries a WHOLE overlay {address: (verdict, note)} applied by ch6_docket_common.apply_whole (the cut's verdict stays above it; a corrected note ends "[whole: what the cut missed]"); the docket (uncommitted) deleted and rewritten with the counts in its header; (b) sitting 4's seven Sifrei rows reread past the cap and the 67 Hebrew rows whole — a correction to the committed ledger an APPENDED section; (c) 3b's rows over 650 reread whole — a correction to the committed docket an appended section, a cell typed from a cut row retyped; (d) 2b's and 1b's rows over 650 the same. Then 4b's RUN 3 as designed.

THE FIX — AS BUILT (2026-09-17, parts (a)-(c)): (a) chapter 6's docket reread whole — 70 of 747 rows corrected, 21 verdicts changed (six rows had carried another row's content; nine rules and five arms missed; the open row's principle at Sanhedrin 4b:12-14, not 4b:2); the docket rewritten with a REREAD WHOLE header, the WHOLE overlays in the parts. (b) sitting 4's Sifrei — the seven spine rows and three outside rows past the 1,500 cap reread: nothing the ledger lacks; the 67 Hebrew rows read whole against the English: the one divergence 36:10 as recorded; an appended section on the ledger. (c) 3b's 82 rows over 650 reread whole: NO verdict changed, three notes would grow; an appended section on the docket. THE MEASURE: at 170 characters one verdict in ten was wrong in substance and two in a hundred sat on the wrong row; at 650 none. (d) 2b (114 rows over 650 of 327) and 1b (215 of 864) are the next run's work; then 4b's RUN 3.

## THE INSTALL HYPOTHESIS — DEUTERONOMY AS THE PROGRAM'S INSTALL (ON THE TABLE, not a ruling; recorded 2026-09-18 on the owner's "yes record it", after his question
## "do you think deuteronomy is a run instruction. why else does it alter old code then create new code?")

THE READING OFFERED: not the run itself but THE INSTALL — the program read back to the generation that will execute it, re-declared for the environment it will run in,
patched where that environment needs it, and written onto the runtime; THE RUN IS JOSHUA (the crossing). Why the book alters old code and then adds new: the target
changed — the first four books are the specification written for a camp under a cloud; Deuteronomy is the same program prepared for the land.

THE EVIDENCE ALREADY MEASURED BY THE WALK (nothing of it typed for the hypothesis; each is a record of sittings 1-5): (1) IT READS THE LOG BACK before it does anything —
the readback's first form, chapters 1-4: forty-two rows and eleven rows of the retelling graded against the tape, the acts told nowhere else written once at their own
day; (2) IT RE-DECLARES THE CODE FOR THE NEW AUDIENCE — chapter 5's ten words with receipts INSIDE them ("as the LORD your God commanded you": the code citing its own
prior giving — the register gate's CHAPTER class), the Sabbath's ground moved from the creation to Egypt (from the designer's ground to the audience's own history),
"that it may go well with you" added; (3) IT PATCHES WHAT THE LAND NEEDS — the cities of refuge east (4:41-43) with the west owed; ahead: the one place, the king, the
courts, the prophet, the war laws; (4) IT WRITES THE PROGRAM ONTO THE RUNTIME — chapter 6 as an install script: on the heart (memory), on the hand and between the eyes
(the person), on the doorposts and the gates (the house), taught to the sons (replication), recited lying down and rising (a heartbeat); the two lines given at the
chapter's own day, STATUTE by form, no marker back to Sinai; (5) THE REGISTRY ALREADY SAYS SO — the book's three daemons (law_opening_speech, law_obey_horeb,
law_hear_o_israel) are installed_by BOOT, not by an act on the tape; (6) THE RECEIPT WITHOUT THE NAME (6:25 "as He commanded us") — the install verifying itself against
the spec in the first person plural; (7) chapter 7's first measurement: the code re-declared with the target's names (SEVEN nations where Exodus had six; both
directions of marriage where Exodus 34:16 barred one; four objects where 34:13 had three; "you shall not covet" moved from the neighbor's house to the idols' silver
and gold).

WHAT WOULD TEST IT (the chapters ahead; nothing of the engine is touched now): the stones at the crossing (27:2-8 — the code copied onto the target), the blessings and
the curses (27:11-28:68 — the exit codes), the covenant at Moab (29 — the install's own covenant, distinct from Horeb's, 28:69), the reading every seven years (31:10-13 —
the reload), the song as a witness (31:19-22, 32), the handoff to Joshua (31:7-8, 23; 34:9), Moses' death outside the target (34). If those compile as install steps
rather than as law cells — writes on the world's own configuration rather than on Israel's ledger — the picture holds; if they compile as ordinary law and narrative,
it falls. THE MACHINE'S OWN CLASSES bear on it: the register gate's headers (4:45 "these are the testimonies" — DAEMONS), the daemons' installed_by field (boot / by an
act), THE LOOP's port (the run's inputs) and its second pass; a class for install steps beside the law cells would be the hypothesis's first engine change, and it is
NOT made until the owner's word after the evidence.

## THE TWO-RUN RULE (owner-ruled 2026-09-18 after 5b's commit 29c189b — "Can we combine runs? These are too short", then "Yes" to the recommendation) — SUPERSEDES THE FOUR-RUN RULE (2026-09-16; its section above stands as history)

THE MEASURE THAT MOVED IT: the four runs came in at 100-200k tokens each against a window of a million; the window that held 5b's run 4 (the chain's wait, the records, the forms), the tutorial's rewrite and the commit used 231k (the owner's /context print: 231.3k of 1m, 23%). THE RULE: a COMPILE sitting is TWO RUNS, a clean compaction point announced after each — RUN A: the rereads (the recovery page, the map's newest section, the memory index; THE_STEPS' compiler block and Step 5's head), the measurements (the recon, the docket scan), THE DESIGN in the map before any code, the probes to FAIL, then THE DOCKET by the union rule (the scan with the ranges named, every row WHOLE in parts on the whole-row instruments, the writer with coverage computed and the cite index) and the map's RUN A paragraph; RUN B: the types by script, the callees' facts printed, the recorder and the stitcher, the runner in parts (the fast checker, the CASES generated from the cells), the literals, the tape to 10/10 with THE REST, checkpoint_check.py --all after the tape, the gates chain in one summary, the records from the sheet in one call (the AS BUILT), the forms copied, the commit message — the commit on the owner's word. A READING sitting is ONE RUN (the measurements and the ink, the rows whole and the ledger, the seat, the chain and the fold, the records). THE SIZES: each run near 300k tokens, never 600k. THE TRIPWIRE: a docket past about 700 rows takes a run of its own (the docket takes the runs its whole reading needs — the whole-row rule stands untouched). The state doc's checkpoint at each run's end names the next run's first step; the recovery page's IN FLIGHT line and the memory index line at each edge as before. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: every shelf row whole; the design before the code; the gates in one chain; the records in one call; the compaction announced, the owner compacting. Chapter 8 runs this way: RUN A its reading as one run (the reading sitting), then the compile's RUN A and RUN B.

THE LESSONS (fifteen, for the next compile): (1) THE RECORDER RUNS WITH THE CACHE OFF — a module restored from the cache never submits: any instrument that
captures a scene's submits needs INK_CACHE=0 (the sweep's and --full's way; a new consumer of the native path, owed to GATES_CHAIN.md's D38 list); (2) the
probes' FAIL run precedes the types — every reader of the world asserts the daemon order against the dispositions, so the types must wait for the probes'
print (6b's order held for a reason); (3) A LITERAL THAT LISTS THE MARKERS MOVES AS SURELY AS ONE THAT COUNTS THEM — before the tape, grep the marker VERSES
in the older checkpoints, not only 'markers N' (the count-literal lesson's fourth class: closes, debits, a status, now a list); (4) the line at the marker's
own verse takes the marker's class (8b's rule, now for a retrograde Deuteronomy line) — the placement is read, never predicted page_order; (5) a line's
subject makes no entity, a write does; (6) THE SIXTH FORM HELD — a stretch is graded against the clock: the markers' days on the running world (DA4, Q22),
the bare world's arithmetic (the runner's CLOCK) and Ta'anit 28b:9's own count agree; the clock read back is a compile rule's test; (7) the docket names the
effect — destruction_halved from the row's own words, the design's provisional name superseded before the types; (8) the callees' print settles the call
forms and the first verses before an assert is typed; (9) a design's tape verse is the LINE's first verse (14:11); (10) the sixth form's SUPPLIED row is
T2's — an act told only in the retelling, written once at its own day by a retrograde marker WITH its write — and the hole's ground (the scan) must
exclude the write once the fold carries it; (11) the stitcher's with_placement() adds the kwarg — an mk code carries none; (12) a count literal in a PROBE moves like one in a checkpoint — the older chapters' 'no marker' probes hold the tape's marker count: grep the probes too
before the chain; (13) THE CACHE'S KEY COVERS EVERY FILE A MODULE READS AT IMPORT — the sequence file was the one left out (its eighteenth slip, found by C2
as the honesty guards were built to find it: nothing set aside); (14) a chain rerun that includes the probes step starts at the tape — the probes read the
tape's live journal and the journal gate consumes it (--from a later step is the only short cut); (15) THE TWO-RUN RULE HELD ON ITS
SECOND COMPILE SITTING — RUN A the design (a clean point), the docket its own run in the same window on the owner's word (a clean point), RUN B this (the
probes, the types, the callees, the runner in parts with the fast checker, the cases, the recorder and the stitcher twice, the literals, the tape twice, the
checkpoint check, the chain five times, the records in one call) — the D series opened at DA1-DA9.

## THE COST AUDIT AND THE THREE RULES (2026-09-20, after 9b's push; owner-ruled "Let's go to 400 a b and c")

THE COST RULES A-B-C (owner-ruled 2026-09-20 after THE COST AUDIT — World/step9/COST_AUDIT_2026-09-20.md, measured from the transcripts: the bill is CACHE WRITES 45% / CACHE READS 37% / OUTPUT 17%; 169 full re-writes of the context after waits past five minutes were a third of the bill; a third of the calls ran past 600k context and carried 57% of the reads; the typed prose under 5%): A. THE CACHE LAW — the cache dies at FIVE MINUTES: no wait past five minutes on a big context. Every long job (the gates chain, the sweep, the positions table, a reading's chain) is LAUNCHED IN THE BACKGROUND AT THE END OF ITS RUN with its readers already written (the records writer, the copier, the message extender parse the chain's prints); the clean point is written and announced; the owner compacts; THE TAIL — a short run on a small context — reads the SUMMARY once, files the demands (a rerun --from the step, waited on the small context), runs the writers, announces. Before any break: the clean point and the compaction first. B. THE 600k CAP (AMENDED 2026-09-20 on the owner's "Let's set the cutoff at 600" — 400k, never past 450k, until then) — a run ends at the clean point nearest 600k, never past 650k (the two-run rule's "near 300k, never 600k" superseded by his word "Let's go to 400"). C. FEWER CALLS — one call per pipeline step; independent reads batched; nothing re-verified that the chain verifies; BATCHING, NEVER SKIPPING (the print-first law stands). THE SITTING SHAPES AMENDED: a COMPILE sitting is TWO RUNS + THE TAIL (RUN A the rereads, the design, the docket — its own run past ~700 rows; RUN B the probes to FAIL, the types, the runner, the tape to 10/10, the writers prepared, the chain LAUNCHED; THE TAIL the summary, the demands, the records, the forms, the message); a READING sitting is ONE run + its tail. Projected: the same work at about a third of the price per chapter.
THE FIRST SITTING UNDER THE RULES: chapter 12's reading (12:1-32) in one run + its tail — the reading's chain launched at the run's end.

THE LESSONS (thirteen): (1) THE GREP DECIDES, AND A BOOLEAN IS NOT A COUNT — a design that predicts "N seats hold the literal" is a prediction; the seats found hold
booleans and move for no reuse; (2) A REGEX'S SILENCE IS NOT A CELL'S — the callees' scan reads only the forms it names; a "no askable cell" verdict is checked against
the cell's own source before an edge is dropped (9b's calendar edge was dropped on the regex's blindness — owed a look at chapter 16); (3) A REUSED EFFECT IS A SECOND
ENTRY (8b's lesson) and needs NO new parameter — the eras table stays in its three cells, read by CALL; (4) THE TABLE IS THE SEVENTH CELL — a functions block counts
what the daemon wraps, not what the design names as cells; (5) TWO RUNNERS' WORDS FOR ONE ROW DIFFER — 'forbidden_forever' against 'banned': an agreement test
normalizes by prefix, never by equality of another runner's string; (6) THE DROP PATTERNS ARE READ FROM THE FAST CHECKER — a store-bound line is any line that names
the store's structures (SG, VC, byw, STORE_), listed by name; (7) THE LINT'S WINDOW IS NINETY CHARACTERS AFTER THE SCRIPT — a long Hebrew literal is glossed piece by
piece; (8) A CASE KIND HAS NO TAPE LINE — a design's "by kind" row on a case kind is a row by CALL; (9) THE GATE'S OPEN BOUND — a daemon given_at a header's own verse
sits outside the header's block; the class is the gate's, the why is ours; (10) THE RECEIPT WITHOUT THE NAME HAS AN ORAL REFERENT — a parameter the cell reads as
data, the written text holding no rite (the code/data separation law's own case; the finder's fourth shape still owed); (11) THE EXAM'S LASHES ARE THE ANSWER SHEET'S
— Mishnah Makkot 3:3's flogged and Makkot 22a's, two persons; (12) AN EFFECT'S COUNT IS READ OFF THE LEDGER, NOT THE REGISTRY'S ROW — the registry named the erection's write; the tape held two on one day (the eighth day's beside it); the one
database's fourteen rows on the-land against seven for the other effects were the sign, misread as folds — a checkpoint's count is typed from the tape's print, a design's is a
prediction; (13) THE TWO-RUN RULE HELD on its fifth compile sitting under the cost rules: RUN A, the docket in three
runs, RUN B with the chain launched at its end, THE TAIL — five clean points, the owner compacting after each. NEXT on the owner's word: the commit; CHAPTER 13's
reading (13:1-19) in one run — the seducer, the dreamer, the seduced city (the DB's 13:1 the English 12:32); on the table: the Decalogue-schema sitting, the
SUPPLIED forms, the calf's day marker, the registry's homograph, the receipt's third and fourth shapes (a gate sitting), THE INSTALL HYPOTHESIS.

- THE TWO RELEASES AT THREE BAVLI SEATS AND THE DECREE ARM (Gittin 36a:14, Kiddushin 38b:3, Moed Katan 2b:17 — Rabbi: "this is the manner of the release: he shall release" (15:2) speaks the land's release and the money's; when the jubilee is not in force the money's release stands by the Sages' decree in remembrance, Gittin 36a:13-36b:1, and the debtor told to sit still, or the court's power over property — 36b:3-4); THE TERRITORY'S OUTSIDE ARM FROM THE VERSE'S OWN CLAUSE (Kiddushin 38b:1, 38b:4 — "because the LORD's release has been proclaimed": in any case; Tosefta Kiddushin 1:10 the twin with the slave's sending as the third exception).
- HILLEL'S PROSBOL (the court's writ) WHOLE AT ITS FOLIO: the reason the verse's own warning (Gittin 36a:11 — 15:9), THE TEXT (Mishnah Sheviit 10:4; Gittin 36a:12), the ground (36a:13 — rabbinic against rabbinic), the land condition and its minimum, its substitutes and the perforated pot (Mishnah 10:6; Gittin 37a:3-7; Tosefta Sheviit 8:10), the writ by speech (37a:6), the date (Tosefta 8:11), the orphans' exemption (37a:2), THE PRESUMPTION "I had one and lost it" (37b:5-8 — a dispute), the scope for all generations (36b:5-10 — Shmuel's "I will nullify it", Rav Nachman's "I will uphold it"); the writ's signatures a dispute (Tosefta 8:9).
- THE MANNER "THE WORD OF THE RELEASE" AT FIVE SEATS (Mishnah Sheviit 10:8 read whole; Gittin 37b:1-2 — the creditor may lift his eyes until "nevertheless"; Shabbat 148b:12 with the edge of a loan made after the year) AND THE OATH RELEASED BY THE SAME WORD (Shevuot 49a:2 — Mishnah Shevuot 7:8; Tosefta Sheviit 8:8 with R. Shimon's arm).
- THE RELEASE'S OBJECT AT THE ANSWER SHEET AND ITS EDGES (Mishnah Sheviit 10:1-2 — the shop's credit and the wage unless made loans, the fines and the court's obligations, the pledge-loan and the notes handed to the court; Tosefta 8:5-7 the shop split by Rabbi, the marriage contract, the lien; THE LIEN'S TWO ARMS Gittin 37a:9-11; THE TEN-YEAR LOAN'S TWO VERSIONS Makkot 3a:15 / 3b:4; THE STIPULATION AGAINST THE RELEASE VOID IN ITS FORM, VALID AS THE DEBTOR'S WAIVER Makkot 3b:7-10; what cannot yet be exacted is not released — Bava Batra 145b:2, Gittin 30a:16; the thirty days from 15:9's doubled name Makkot 3b:11-14).
- THE COUNT RENEWED AT EZRA'S RETURN AND THE JUBILEE'S CONDITION (Arakhin 32b:10 — as at Joshua's arrival they counted sabbaticals and jubilees; 30:5's "your fathers possessed" 32b:11; THE JUBILEE NULLIFIED WHEN REUBEN, GAD AND HALF MANASSEH WERE EXILED — "to all its inhabitants", in their arrangement, 32b:15-17; THE FIFTIETH COUNTED TO ORDER THE SABBATICALS with the jubilee's laws not in force 32b:18; the fiftieth's arithmetic two arms 33a:1, Rosh Hashanah 9a:1), THE JUBILEE'S ONSET at the New Year with the slaves crowned till Yom Kippur (Rosh Hashanah 8b:8-12; Arakhin 28b:7 — the sabbatical at its END), the pierced slave's jubilee at Jeremiah's seat (Arakhin 33a:2-4 — two persons in 34:14).

Elazar ben Azarya and R. Shimon: "the Torah speaks in the language of men" — the dissenting arms; Ketubot 67b:11 the same); 15:4's "no needy among you" A PRECEDENCE RULE for one's own property (Bava Metzia 30b:1, 33a:10; Sanhedrin 64b:15); 15:4 and 15:11 TWO LIVES (Taanit 21a:2-4) and Shmuel's unchanged world (Berakhot 34b:20; Shabbat 63a:10).

THE FINDS OF KIDDUSHIN 14b-22b (carried into the exam file's "## The finds" after D1's):
- THE THREE CASES OF THE HEBREW SLAVE AT THEIR SUGYA (Kiddushin 14b:7-15b:4): the analogy 'hired worker' / 'hired worker' (I2 — Leviticus 25:40 with 15:18) joins the self-seller to the court's sale; the baraita's four differences (14b:9-11 — the term six or more, the awl, the severance, the Canaanite maidservant) against R. Elazar's 'no difference'; the teacher who rejects the analogy is Rabbi (15a:23-15b:4 — the gentile's slave redeemed 'by any of these' relatives, never by six years); THE GENTILE'S SLAVE'S REDEEMERS (15b:5-14 — R. Yosei HaGelili by the verse PRECEDING (E28), R. Akiva by the following, the Rabbis every redemption to freedom; the dispute a matter of reason 15b:10-11).
- THE SEVERANCE GIFT'S PERSONS, MEASURE AND FEATURE: 'to him' — not the self-seller (15a:6), not his creditor (Tutai 16b:16; 15a:7 — not his heirs refused, a hired worker's wage passes); the sendings extended by 'you shall not send' and 'when you send' (16b:19), 'from you' excluding the fugitive and the one who deducts with R. Meir's arm (16b:20, 16b:17); THE MEASURE THREE ARMS WITH THEIR GROUNDS (17a:5 — five per kind by 'empty' / 'empty' with the firstborn 17a:7-8; thirty by 'giving' / 'giving' with the gored slave 17a:10; fifty by the valuations and 'poverty' / 'poverty' 17a:13-14; the selection rule 'grasped too much, grasped nothing' 17a:12; R. Meir's total not less 17a:6); THE FEATURE the category of blessing — money out (R. Shimon) or mules out (R. Eliezer ben Yaakov), 17a:16-17b:1; THE DOUBLED VERB 'grant, you shall grant' in any case (17b:2) against R. Elazar ben Azarya's plain reading — 'the Torah speaks in the language of men' (17b:3); the maidservant's gift to her father while he lives (16b:11-13), her brothers excluded (16b:14).
- THE EXITS' TABLES AT THE ANSWER SHEET AND ITS GEMARA: Mishnah Kiddushin 1:2 whole (14b:2); the modes' grounds — money from the gentile's sale and the maidservant's redemption (14b:3-8), the document from 'another wife' or 'as the men slaves do' (16a:2-8), no possession (16a:5); THE DEDUCTION AND THE BODY OWNED (Rava 16a:13 — a waiver releases nothing, a document of manumission needed; the price the lower reckoning 20a:9-12, 20b:4-6 'expounded like Sinai'; no partial redemption 20b:8-9); the four ways with severance, three and three (16b:3-8, 16b:17-18); Reish Lakish's father's-death exit refuted (16a:14-16b:10); the two tables of 18a:5 with Rav Sheshet's designated maidservant (18a:6); THE FUGITIVE AND THE SICK (16b:21-17a:4 — sick four years as six; needlework no completion).
- THE PIERCED AND THE JUBILEE: 'forever' UNTIL THE JUBILEE (15a:21-22; 21b:4 — the master's lifetime, the jubilee's forever); the two verses both needed (15a:19-20); THE PIERCED SERVES NO HEIR and the slave serves the son, not the daughter (17b:4-13 — the son stands in his father's place for the designation and the field); THE MAIDSERVANT NEVER PIERCED (15a:3, 15a:5, 15a:18 'man') — 122:9's DISAGREES row against Exodus 21:7 RESOLVED as DATA; 'LIKEWISE' REACHES THE GIFT, NOT THE AWL (17b:10-12 — R. Padda's two conclusions from 'you shall DO').
- THE AWL'S TOOLS AND THE EAR AT THEIR OWN FOLIO (21b:5-22b:5): R. Yosei son of R. Yehuda's amplification-restriction (anything taken in the hand but a corrosive) against Rabbi's GENERAL-PARTICULAR-GENERAL (I6 — metal), 21b:5-10; 'THE awl' the large awl by the article (21b:11); THE RIGHT EAR by 'ear' / 'ear' with the leper (15a:1 — the design's labeled transfer at its Bavli seat); THE UPPER EAR THROUGH THE CARTILAGE because a priest-slave is not pierced lest he be blemished — 'and he shall return to his own family' (21b:7, 21b:12; Bekhorot 37b:12-14 the twin); through the ear until the door (22b:1-2); the door upright and attached (22b:3); the ear's and the door's homilies (22b:4-5).
- THE TWO SAYINGS AND THE RITE'S CONDITIONS: says and repeats, while a slave, at the last peruta (22a:3-6; 15a:4-5); the mutual love and the master's house, illness in either (22a:7-8), both ill an open dilemma (22a:9); THE BOARD 'with you' — not fine bread against coarse, aged wine against new, soft bedding against straw, 'one who acquires a Hebrew slave acquires a master' (20a:14-15, 22a:10); THE NIGHT'S SERVICE the Canaanite maidservant, not labor (15a:11-13 — 123:1's double hire RESOLVED), for a priest-slave Rav permits and Shmuel forbids with Rav Nachman's proof (21b:13-16); THE FAMILY FED (22a:11-13 — 'he and his children with him', 'his wife shall go out with him').

Yosei son of R. Yehuda's peruta, 'designate her' read 'inform her' (19a:7-19b:2); the stipulation against designation (19b:12-14); the sale to flawed lineage and to relatives (19b:15-20a:5); THE THIEF'S SALE 'for his theft' — the principal, once, R. THE LESSONS (⚠): (1) A COUNT ASSERT IN A FILING SCRIPT GOES STALE WHEN A LATER SET ADDS AN EDGE — the second set's `== 33` fell at the fourth set's run: a filing script asserts `>=` on the counts an earlier set fixed, or reads the count from the file at each set; (2) THE CENSUS'S HOMOGRAPHS ARE CONSONANTAL — sabbath, olah, firstborn and rain all tripped on the consonants of another word in these chapters (the census's section C names the value that spells the name; the disposition is FALSE with the homograph named); (3) A SCAN'S DECLARED LIST IS READ FROM ITS SOURCE — the tape's DC4 compares the runner's own RAIN_VOCAB (a registry scan at import) with a declared list: excluding a name in the tape's copy leaves the runner's scan wide; the exclusion goes where the scan is (the third tape run); (4) A DETACHED `( … &)` JOB GIVES NO NOTIFICATION — a long foreground command backgrounds itself past its timeout and notifies; an `until [ -f DONE ]` loop in the background does the same for a wrapper's DONE file; (5) THE DAEMON GATE READS LITERAL SUBMITS ONLY — twenty `w.submit({...})` calls typed out, never built from a table (15b's lesson restated for a four-chapter runner); (6) THE KIN COUNTS ARE ONE RUN'S — count_scan reads the largest `source` in run_ledger, never the whole fold; (7) FOUR CHAPTERS ARE ONE RUNNER IN SEVEN PARTS — the cells four to a part in halves, the readback in five blocks, the daemon in three, the cases generated as an eighth: the heredoc stays under the output limit at every part; (8) THE TWO-RUN RULE HELD FOR A LEAN COMPILE OVER FOUR CHAPTERS (89 timed steps, 6298 machine seconds; the chain 2063 s of them) — the types at RUN B's head cost nothing the window could not hold.

THE FINDS are the runner's cells against the forty-four rows: THE LOST THING returned and never hidden from, the beast raised with its owner (Bava Metzia 2:7-10 — the claimant's marks, the finder's care, the wages of the raising); the garments and the nest — a man's gear on a woman, the mother sent from the eggs and the fledglings (Chullin 12:2-3), the parapet with the bloodguilt on the house; the mixtures — the vineyard's seed, the ox and the ass, wool and linen, the tassels on the four corners; THE SLANDERED BRIDE with the plotting witnesses by CALL (Ketubot 3:1, 3:5, 4:3 — the fine, the seducer's marriage, the father's rights), the girl written as a boy at her twelve seats; the adulterers strangled (Sanhedrin 11:1), the betrothed girl in the city and in the field, the seducer's fifty; THE ASSEMBLY — the father's wife, the crushed and the cut, the bastard, Ammon and Moab forever and Edom and Egypt at the third generation (Yevamot 8:2-3); THE CAMP — the night's chance and the reading of the Shema (Berakhot 3:5; Zavim 2:3), the spade on the weapon; the escaped slave not returned, the harlot's hire and the dog's price barred from the house (Temurah 6:2-3), the interest not bitten from a brother (Bava Metzia 5:10); THE VOW not delayed past the three festivals (Rosh Hashanah 1:1), refraining permitted; the laborer in the vineyard and the standing grain — the hand, never the vessel or the sickle; THE DIVORCE — the writ, the sending, the second husband and the first barred from returning (Gittin 2:4, 3:1, 8:1, 9:10 — the three arms of "some unseemly thing"; Kiddushin 1:1 the taking); the newlywed's year (Sotah 8:4), the millstone as a life, the kidnapper; the leprosy's rule and MIRIAM REMEMBERED; the pledge taken outside and returned by sunset (Bava Metzia 9:13), the widow's garment, the hireling's wage before the sun; FATHERS NOT FOR SONS (Sanhedrin 3:4 — the relatives barred as witnesses), the stranger's judgment, the forgotten sheaf and the gleanings of the olive and the vine (Peah 4:6, 6:6, 7:2); THE FORTY LASHES less one and the count (Makkot 3:10, 3:15); the muzzle; THE LEVIRATE — the brothers dwelling together, the widow's declaration and the shoe loosed in the holy tongue (Yevamot 1:1, 2:1, 3:9, 4:13, 10:1, 12:1, 12:3, 12:6; Sotah 7:2), the house of the unshod named; THE WRESTLERS' WIFE and her hand (Bava Kamma 8:1, 8:3 — humiliation as money by the import of 25:11-12); the weights and the measures whole and just (Bava Batra 5:10-11); AMALEK remembered, blotted and never forgotten — Exodus 17's line by CALL.

THE LESSONS (⚠): (1) A KIN'S REGISTRY-KEY SCAN TRIPS AT IMPORT, BEFORE ANY RUN — the census of `for k in _FXV if 'x' in k` forms belongs before the fast checker's first run (the rain's fifth key); (2) THE INK MODULE'S COPIED ASSERTS CARRY NO GLOSSES — a transformer wraps every Hebrew literal with its English (the ink forms' own flags a debt); (3) A Q-STYLE CELL'S KEYS ARE READ FROM ITS SOURCE, an ask-style cell wants (case, data) — the probe's fallback form tells which; (4) A FACT TYPED AS A TUPLE INDEX ON A DICT FAILS AT THE ASK CHECKER, not the fast checker — both run before the generator; (5) A GROUPED `if ask in (...)` BRANCH HIDES ITS ASKS from the generator's regex — one branch per ask; (6) THE FOLD AFTER THE TAPE'S FIRST RUN CARRIES THE NEW ROWS — before the second run every older runner's import-time scan is censused against the NEW NAMES (the census's section A intersected with the spec; three runners widened by name) AND an older runner's KIN_EXPECTED counts move with a reuse — a fourth scan form; (7) A REFERENCE ROW'S TAPE SEAT IS THE LINE'S FIRST VERSE (28:64's witnesses at 4:26 inside the 4:25-31 line); (8) A DERIVED CHECKPOINT KEEPS ITS MODEL'S HELPERS (DL1's day by D() read the creation count's year; DK1's ex.date); (9) THE REUSES MOVE THE EARLIER CHECKPOINTS AND THE PROBES — thirteen checkpoints and eight probe lines retyped from the print with the since-note, each miss read first, the changed element alone by ast; (10) THE DESIGN'S HOLE_WORDS MUST CARRY EVERY OLDER WORD LIST THE TAPE SCANS (DA6's neck found the iron yoke — excluded by name in 16b's form); (11) AN ALIAS THROUGH A SUBSCRIPT (X = M.DATA['k']) KEEPS ITS SHARING GROUP ONLY IN A WHOLE HARVEST — after editing an older runner, clear the import cache before the chain or C6 falls (the partial re-harvest beside cached neighbours records a fresh blob); (12) A GATE'S LIVE EDGE IS `alias.name(` — an accessor that takes the module as an argument hides the call; (13) THE TWO-RUN RULE HELD FOR A LEAN COMPILE OVER THREE CHAPTERS WITH FIVE UNITS (81 timed steps, 9021 machine seconds; the chain's two passes 896 + 2950 s of them) — the tail in RUN B's window at 305k, no compaction needed.

THE LESSONS (⚠): (1) A COMPILE'S RUN A AFTER A READING'S TAIL IN ONE WINDOW TAKES THE COMPACTION FIRST (the cap passed at 725k); (2) A MARKER SITTING IS BIGGER THAN A STATUTE SITTING — its RUN B splits into two windows (the types, the tools and the runner to its first graded run; then the tape, the census and the retypes): RUN B ran to the machine's compaction; (3) THE MARKER MOVES EVERY EARLIER PROBE AND CHECKPOINT that counts the markers OR ASSERTS THE COUNTER'S DAY (Q23 and Q26 assert the tape's last day) — both classes are counted at the design, and THE READBACK SUITE RUNS RIGHT AFTER THE TAPE'S 10/10, before the chain, since the tape's own run never runs the probes; (4) A MARKER'S WALK FIRES THE TIMERS DUE IN IT — the sabbath's and the month's over the walked days (six fired, six re-armed, six writes; the design's +0); (5) count_scan COUNTS THE WORLD'S ENTRIES, not one ledger's; (6) A TWO-LETTER ALIAS COLLIDES WITH A HELPER; (7) THE KIN CORROBORATES THE SHELF'S DATE TWICE (Seder Olam 10:2 in chukat, Kiddushin 38a in exodus_story — the 7th of Adar on two ledgers); (8) THE HAKHEL READS THE TAPE — Sotah 7:8's seven portions are lines on the tape, every one a registered kind; (9) THE EVENTS' PLACEMENT CLASSES AT A MARKED DAY ARE READ FROM THE STITCHER'S PRINT, never predicted; (10) CT6'S TWO ARITHMETICS agree only on a fire day; (11) A LATER REUSE MOVES EARLIER RUNNERS' LITERALS — an entity list, a KIN_EXPECTED count — beyond 18b's scan census: the fast checker's import is the second reader, the sweep the third; (12) THE GATE'S LIVE EDGE IS `alias.name(` AND A COMMENT CARRYING THE FORM SATISFIES IT FALSELY — the facts CALL the cell; (13) THE EVENTS' CASE SOURCES ARE DOUBLE-QUOTED WHERE AN APOSTROPHE SITS — a regex over them takes both quote forms; (14) A PROBE'S OWN CUT ENDS BEFORE THE ANSWER (q20's nine characters — 13b's lesson 1 inside a probe); (15) THE ONE DATABASE HOLDS EVERY TAPE RUN'S WRITES — a count over it is not the live world's (20 against 4; the ledger is replayed from the events); (16) AN ELEMENT INSIDE A GENERATOR EXPRESSION HIDES FROM THE AST WALKER — the print of a rerun shows it; after a retype by ast the probe suite runs before the chain; (17) THE CACHE LAW WAS BROKEN ABOUT TWENTY TIMES — every check of 3-9 minutes at 300-600k re-read the context cold: a marker sitting's checks run in ONE background wrapper per phase with their readers written first, or the window stays small; (18) THE TAIL OPENS ON HIS WORD — after any compaction the rereads and the report, then "Go" (the harness's continuation is not his word); (19) THE POSITIONS TABLE AT FOUR WORKERS IS KILLED BY THE MEMORY WATCHDOG WHEN OTHER SESSIONS SHARE THE MACHINE — two workers outside the chain, then --from checkpoint (13b's form); (20) THE TWO-RUN RULE DID NOT HOLD for a lean compile with a marker (89 timed steps, 16256 machine seconds; the chain's passes 1210 + 8554 s of them).
